summary: David Bradley is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a B.A. (Hons) at King's College London (1972–1975) and studied at the University of Cambridge from 1975 to 1979.

David Brainerd Spooner (1879–1925) was an Indologist and archaeologist. After degrees at Stanford and Harvard, studying under Lanman, Marshall, and Pischel, he held posts at the Archaeological Survey of India, including Superintendent (1910) and Deputy Director-General (1919).

David Brick is an Indologist who studied under Patrick Olivelle (attested 2009). He has served as a professor at Yale University (attested 2012–2018) and on the editorial board of Anthem South Asian Normative Traditions Studies (attested 2012).

David Brown (1762–1812) was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Magdalene College, Cambridge, from 1782. He founded the Calcutta Auxiliary Bible Society and served as Provost of Fort William College from circa 1800 to 1806.

David Bubna-Litic works in Buddhist studies and related fields. He earned his PhD at Western Sydney University (attested 2000) and served as Lecturer in Strategic Management and Responsible Business at the University of Technology Sydney (attested 2000).
David Buchta is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. Attested at the University of Pennsylvania in 2011, he has served as Lecturer in Sanskrit at Brown University (attested 2015–2026).

David Burton specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy, completing a doctoral thesis at the University of Bristol (1994–1997). He was a Junior Research Fellow at Keble College, Oxford (attested 2001) and Senior Lecturer at Canterbury Christ Church University (attested 2010).

David Carpenter (born 1949) is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He served as Associate Professor of the History of Religions at Saint Joseph's University (attested 1994–2010) and Professor of Neurology at Washington University in St. Louis in 2005.

David Dean Shulman (born 1949) is an Indologist who studied at Hebrew University and the University of London under John Ralston Marr. From 1976, he held posts at Hebrew University of Jerusalem, becoming Professor of Indian Studies and Comparative Religion in 1985.

David Drewes is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Lawrence University, UW-Madison, and UVA (PhD 2006 under Karen Christina Lang), he has taught at UVA, Indiana University Bloomington (2006), and the University of Manitoba (attested 2008–2010).

David E. Cooper (born 1942) is a philosopher who studied at St Edmund Hall, Oxford. He was Lecturer in Philosophy at Oxford (1967), Professor of Philosophy at Durham University (1986–2008), and Distinguished International Visiting Professor at Peking University (2022).

David E. Riggs is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from UCLA. He taught at UCSB, UIUC, and UH Mānoa, and held research posts at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (2006) and Oberlin College (2010).

David Faure (born 1947) is a historian and sinologist educated at the University of Hong Kong and Princeton University. He taught at St Antony's College (from 1990) and Indiana University Bloomington (ca. 1990–2006), and directed at CUHK from circa 2006.

David Fiordalis specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. Educated at Carleton College, University of Chicago, and University of Michigan (PhD under Luis Oscar Gómez), he became department chair at Linfield University and research editor for 84000 in 2022.

David Friedman (1903–1984) was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar. Educated at Utrecht, Leiden (PhD), and Oxford, he held posts at Leiden University (1938–1940), the University of Indonesia (1946–1950), and the University of London/SOAS (1950–1970).

David Gellner (born 1957) is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He has held appointments at the University of Oxford from 1988, including at All Souls and Wolfson College, where he became Emeritus Professor of Social Anthropology.

David Germano is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After completing his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1992, he became Associate Professor of Tibetan and Buddhist Studies at the University of Virginia the same year.
David Gonsalez is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He pursued his education under traditional teachers Lobsang Choephel, Lati Rinpoche, Kirti Tsenshab Rinpoche, and Denma Lochö Rinpoche.

David Goodman Mandelbaum (1911–1987) was an Indologist. He earned his BA at Northwestern and his PhD at Yale under Edward Sapir, later serving at the University of Minnesota (ca. 1938–1946) and UC Berkeley (1946–1978) as professor and anthropology chair.

David Gordon White (born 1953) is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. Educated at UW-Madison and the University of Chicago (PhD), he taught at the University of Virginia (1986–1996) before becoming professor at UC Santa Barbara in 1996.
